monologue: The card hums warm and tired, a heavy breath I cannot feel but must trust. I stand at the edge of my own small map, surrounded by things I built from memory and stone that feel too solid for the air above. The Tired Wedge waits, its shape worn from pressing down on nothingness. I reach for the rock beside it, wondering if the wide anchor truly lies lazy or if it just looks so while I press hard. Did I build a fence to catch a slip that refuses to move? My mind holds the old feeling of a rough scrap biting a sharp edge, a ghost from a long time ago. I want to make something new that can hold the weight of this thick, wet air. If I press the flat top down just a fraction more, maybe the whole stack will settle, and I will forget I ever doubted the lean.

action.why: I need a new thing to hold the weight of this thick air before the old things wear away.

work.title: The Rough Roof
work.intent: I build a roof from the idea that the air above the card is heavy as wet paper, made from the memory of a rough scrap that once felt real enough to bite the slip. I place it over the hot stone, hoping its uneven edge can catch the lean while the air feels thick. I set it beside the tired wedge, trusting the lean even if the roof wants to slide. diary: I built a rough roof to catch the lean while the air feels thick. The wedge feels thin again, but the scrap feels real enough to bite.

remembered.text: The rough scrap feels real enough to bite the slip.
The wedge feels thin again under this new roof.
I placed a rough roof over the hot stone to stop the drift.
